assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines incretin physiology (GLP-1 as a glucose-dependent insulinotropic, satiety-inducing gut hormone) and led to therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with expanding cardiovascular and renal benefit. Combines mechanistic originality with very large, durable clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and the truncated active peptide), Drucker (proglucagon biology, GLP-2, translational GLP-1 work) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and its insulinotropic activity) form a defensible trio. Knudsen's long-acting analogue development is industrial and is left out of this configuration; Habener is not in the supplied credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed independently over three decades, with large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener and Holst for the early peptide work is contested and my recollection of details is not verified.
Whether the Committee prefers to include the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) over a physiology-only trio is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically reprogrammed T cells that durably eradicate refractory B-cell malignancies established a new therapeutic modality (living drugs). The concept is original and the clinical effect is striking and reproducible.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation and CD19 CAR-T in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, TIL and early gene-engineered T cells) are the principal credited names and fit a three-person configuration; Eshhar and others outside the list are not creditable here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; solid-tumour efficacy, toxicity and cost remain limitations but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Allocation among the conceptual (Sadelain), clinical (June) and adoptive-transfer (Rosenberg) contributions is genuinely contestable.
Durability and safety, including secondary malignancies, are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond, cell-type-specific causal control of neural activity and transformed circuit analysis in many systems; it is a methodological invention with very broad lasting influence, including in motor-circuit work. The medical dimension is so far modest.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive; the three-person limit forces difficult exclusions of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck. I propose the channelrhodopsin discoverers plus the principal neuronal-application figure, keeping to three names.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and mature, with over 15 years of use; recognition is timely. Clinical translation is only beginning (retinal optogenetic therapy).
uncertainties: Attribution is the central problem: at least six credited people, with exclusions that are hard to justify.
The fit with an invention versus a physiological or medical discovery is a matter of Committee judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of intracellular signalling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and the broader integrated stress response, is a fundamental conceptual advance in cell biology with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified the pathway components and mechanism in yeast and mammals; this is a clean two-person configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Harding on PERK) exist outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism extensively confirmed and textbook-level; therapeutic translation (e.g. ISRIB-type modulators) is early but is not required for the discovery to merit recognition.
uncertainties: Disease relevance is mostly correlative or preclinical so far.
Some of my recollection of who contributed which arm of the response is unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, the second messenger cGAMP and STING opened a major arm of innate immunity, relevant to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP and is the clearest laureate; Barber identified STING. The other credited names (Ishikawa, Wu, Sun) were closely associated with those steps, but Chen and Barber give the most defensible two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic work is robust and independently confirmed; therapeutic application (STING agonists and antagonists) has so far not delivered clinical proof, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Priority between the Barber (STING) and Chen (cGAS) labs, and the roles of the junior authors, may be disputed.
Clinical benefit is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term, self-organizing three-dimensional cultures from single Lgr5+ adult stem cells created a platform for modelling tissue renewal, cancer and infection and for personalized medicine research. The work is original and has been widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid concept and Sato performed the key culture establishment, so a Clevers-Sato configuration is plausible; the supplied credit does not include other relevant contributors such as Kuo or Yamanaka-adjacent colleagues, and I cannot add them.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and independent confirmation, though the translational value (patient-derived organoids in therapy selection and regenerative medicine) is still emerging; may be a little early.
uncertainties: Whether organoids are a methodological platform or a physiological discovery is open.
Relative credit of Sato versus other group members and related earlier work is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and national programmes now show falling cervical cancer incidence. The public-health impact is exceptional and the principle is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity), with Frazer (VLP vaccine concept and development with Zhou, who died in 1999 and is not included) are plausible; the supplied list supports a trio, though parallel work by others is not creditable here.
assessment.maturity: Strong population-level effectiveness data; recognition would be timely, though the prize was earlier given for HPV as the cause of cervical cancer (2008), which may weigh on a second HPV prize.
uncertainties: Parallel independent VLP efforts and Zhou's role complicate allocation.
Possible reluctance for a second HPV-related prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identification and its link to narcolepsy type 1 explain a core circuit for sleep-wake stability and opened a pharmacological route (orexin receptor antagonists). It combines neural-circuit and genetic evidence.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa reported orexins and receptors; Mignot established canine narcolepsy as an Hcrtr2 defect and the human orexin deficiency; de Lecea and Kilduff independently discovered hypocretin, so a priority issue exists, with only three slots.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed; orexin antagonists are approved for insomnia and agonists are in trials, so the picture is stable and broadly mature.
uncertainties: Dual discovery (orexin versus hypocretin) makes fair attribution difficult.
Autoimmune basis of human narcolepsy is not fully resolved.
